subject: Latency floor & throughput safety-net — dedicated pool SLA amendment (AstraNova)
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@astranova.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sethi <priya.s@astranova.com>, legal@astranova.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: add "latency floor" + throughput safety-net to Dedicated SLA

Diego — thanks for the runthrough yesterday. We love the Dedicated pool performance but need one more safety measure before CD signing: visibility and remediation if 99.9th percentile tail latency exceeds 450ms for more than 15 min in a 24h window for our production endpoints.

Specifically asking for: a contractual "latency floor" (tail threshold) that will trigger either an automatic traffic shift to a warm standby pool or a crediting mechanism. Second ask: a defined throughput safety-net (reserved headroom) that prevents noisy-tenant preemption during our daily peak hour.

Attached is a short draft of clause language our legal team suggested (redlines). Happy to take your suggestions.

— Raj
AstraNova Labs

Attachments: redline_comments_astranova_marked.docx (word doc, 24 KB)

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@astranova.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: add "latency floor" + throughput safety-net to Dedicated SLA

Raj — appreciate the clear ask and the redlines. I want to align on two practical options we can operationalize without changing the core Dedicated model too much: 

1) Latency attenuation clause + auto-warm-standby: if tail latency >450ms for >=15m, we route new requests for affected route(s) to a pre-warmed fallback pool (same region, identical model family) until metrics stabilize. Fallback is rate-limited to preserve stability.

2) Throughput safety-net (headroom carveout): we reserve a small isolated headroom pool equal to 10% of your committed capacity during your peak window; it will not be subject to tenant preemption and will absorb sudden bursts.

Operational questions for you: can you confirm your daily peak window (local time) and whether 10% headroom aligns with your internal tolerance? Also looping in Marissa and Karthik to validate capacity and billing implications.

I attached an internal headroom model and a first-pass SLA amendment draft.

— Diego
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ANL_SLA_amendment_draft_v2.pdf (pdf, 72 KB); headroom_modeling_20270629.xlsx (spreadsheet, 56 KB)

From: Priya Sethi <priya.s@astranova.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@astranova.com>, legal@astranova.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 13:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: add "latency floor" + throughput safety-net to Dedicated SLA

Diego — thanks. Our production peak is 14:00–16:00 PT weekdays. 10% sounds reasonable as a starting point, but we need clarity on how credits would be calculated if the fallback is used (we'll defer to Legal on exact language). Two product constraints for us: we cannot accept any traffic redirection that can change model family (must remain same model family), and warm standby needs to be warmed with KV cache warming (cold fallback increases latency).

Raj + legal: please see Diego's draft and the headroom model — I'm ok to proceed if Redwood can guarantee same-model-family fallback and a KV cache warming plan.

— Priya
Director of ML Ops, AstraNova Labs

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Latency floor & throughput safety-net — Dedicated pool SLA amendment (AstraNova)

Team — quick feasibility notes from ops/R&D:
- Same-model-family fallback: feasible. We'll provision a warm replica pool with the same quantization/config. Need to confirm model size to size warm cache.
- KV cache warming: we can implement prefix prefetching for a targeted keyset; lead time ~48–72 hours to adapt pipelines for warm-up scripts and test.
- Headroom carveout (10%): operationally simple as a reserved slice. Billing: billable as part of committed capacity but with an agreed crediting scheme if safety-net is used more than X hours/month.

Question for Sales: do we propose a credit-based remediation or an SLA "escalation + manual mitigation" path for first 3 months? Credits are simpler contractually and auditably.

— Marissa
Head of Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@astranova.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sethi <priya.s@astranova.com>, legal@astranova.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency floor & throughput safety-net — Dedicated pool SLA amendment (AstraNova)

Thanks Marissa — agree that credits are the cleanest. Legal suggests this shape: if fallback is invoked cumulatively > 2 hours/month, Redwood issues a service credit equal to 5% of that month's committed capacity fee per each additional hour (capped at 50% monthly). We also want an explicit statement that the fallback respects same-model-family and KV warming.

Also asking whether the headroom can be scheduled (e.g., 14:00–16:00 PT weekdays) to avoid 24/7 reserved costs. If scheduled, what's the minimum guaranteed window per day (we'd like 2 hours consistent).

— Raj

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@astranova.com>, Priya Sethi <priya.s@astranova.com>, legal@astranova.com
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency floor & throughput safety-net — Dedicated pool SLA amendment (AstraNova)

Team — alignment and next steps:
1) Schedule: we can carve out a scheduled headroom pool for 14:00–16:00 PT weekdays. Minimum daily guaranteed window is 2 hours; outside that window the headroom remains reclaimable but we will not preempt your committed requests during the scheduled window.
2) Crediting: agree to the credit band Raj proposed as a negotiation baseline; Sales/Finance will draft the exact formula and cap language for DocuSign.
3) KV warming: Ops will run a KV prefetch job prior to the scheduled window; long-term we can integrate a warming API. Lead time for initial rollout: 10 business days for validation.
4) DocuSign: I'll upload a DocuSign-ready amendment with Marissa's operational notes and your redlines by EOD Monday.

Marissa/Karthik/Rishi — can you confirm the headroom sizing in the attached model (I increased to 12% reflecting expected burstiness) and call out any platform limitations we should document?

Raj/Priya — once we reconcile the numeric headroom and the crediting formula I'll circulate the redline-ready doc.

Thanks — Diego
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ANL_SLA_amendment_draft_v2.pdf (updated), headroom_modeling_20270629.xlsx (updated)
